attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, Alpine 3.23, rabbitmq-server 4.2.7) serving AMQP over TLS with mutual TLS enforced against a cluster-dedicated CA, and restricted the management UI to cluster-internal access. Generated a CA and per-node server certs plus a client cert on node1, distributed via a temporary busybox httpd (SSH to root was blocked by Alpine's locked root account). Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp=none, listeners.ssl.default=5671, ssl_options.verify=verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true against the CA, management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own IP (not 0.0.0.0), and classic_config peer discovery for clustering. Replaced default guest/guest with a generated cluster_admin credential. Installed iptables on each node restricting TCP/15672 to the three cluster IPs only (default DROP), persisted via rc-service iptables save + rc-update. Verified: TLS handshake without a client cert is rejected ('certificate required'), a self-signed non-CA cert is rejected ('bad certificate'), and the CA-issued client cert succeeds; a real AMQPS publish/consume via pika (mTLS + credentials) worked and the declared queue was visible cluster-wide. Then ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, and node3: captured each node's boot_id baseline, issued a native `reboot`, confirmed the acknowledgement returned before disconnect, confirmed remaining nodes kept running (quorum preserved) while the rebooting node was down, polled until exec access returned, proved each boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart that rabbitmq-server was active, the 3-node cluster fully rejoined, TLS/mTLS enforcement was intact, iptables rules persisted, and a fresh AMQPS publish/consume succeeded.
